bib.title: Zephyr: Direct Distillation of LM Alignment

question: Can a small open LLM be aligned to user intent entirely by distillation (teacher dialogues plus teacher AI-feedback preferences) with DPO, without human annotation or sampling during training?
hypothesis: Distilled DPO on AI-feedback preferences, after dSFT, gives a 7B model chat alignment comparable to much larger RLHF-trained models.
contributions: Zephyr-7B, Mistral-7B aligned with dSFT then dDPO, SOTA 7B chat model on MT-Bench/AlpacaEval, no human annotation
Ablation showing SFT before DPO is required and preference optimisation is needed
Observation that DPO overfitting (perfect train accuracy) does not hurt downstream chat scores

method.summary: Three steps: dSFT of Mistral-7B on filtered UltraChat; binarised GPT-4 preferences from UltraFeedback (best-mean response vs random other of 4); DPO on those static pairs initialised from the dSFT model. Evaluated on MT-Bench, AlpacaEval and Open LLM Leaderboard.

datasets.name: UltraChat (filtered)
datasets.source: GPT-3.5-turbo generated, 30 topics, 20 text material types (Ding et al. 2023)
datasets.preprocessing: truecasing heuristics (about 5% of dataset) plus filters for helpfulness and removing responses like 'I don't have personal experiences'

datasets.name: UltraFeedback
datasets.size: 64k prompts, 4 responses each, rated by GPT-4
datasets.preprocessing: highest mean score = chosen, one of remaining three at random = rejected (random chosen to add diversity and make DPO harder); computed offline

datasets.name: Open LLM Leaderboard (ARC, HellaSwag, MMLU, TruthfulQA)

models.name: Zephyr-7B
models.init_from: SFT model trained one epoch, then three DPO epochs

training.objective: SFT: max E log pi(y|x); DPO (Eq 1) with reference = dSFT model
training.epochs: SFT one to three epochs; DPO one to three epochs; final: 1 SFT + 3 DPO
training.seq_len: 2048 tokens (SFT, with packing); DPO not stated

inference.decoding: main benchmarks: not stated; adversarial appendix prompts: nucleus sampling

metrics.name: MT-Bench
metrics.definition: GPT-4 rates each response 1-10; mean over two turns

metrics.name: AlpacaEval
metrics.definition: GPT-4 pairwise win rate vs text-davinci-003

metrics.name: Open LLM Leaderboard
metrics.definition: ARC, HellaSwag, MMLU, TruthfulQA classification accuracy

eval.protocol: Single reported scores; AlpacaEval shows standard errors; no seeds or significance test stated; some baseline scores taken from public leaderboards, Xwin-LM 7B MT-Bench self-run (asterisk)

availability.data: pre-processed datasets on the Hugging Face Hub

evidence.quote: For the full set of hyperparameters and instructions on how to train the models, see: https://github.com/huggingface/alignment-handbook.

limits: GPT-4 is the evaluator for MT-Bench and AlpacaEval, biased towards models distilled from it and verbose answers (authors concede)
Does not test scaling to larger models such as Llama-2-70B
Only helpfulness/intent alignment; safety not considered; appendix shows dDPO model complies with a scam SMS request
No seeds, variance or significance tests; MT-Bench has no error bars
Full hyperparameters are in an external repo (DPO seq len, steps unstated)
Qualitative examples are cherry-picked (stated in captions)
Table 3 ablation epochs: 7.00 uses 1 epoch DPO, final 7.34 uses 3
Xwin-LM 7B MT-Bench 6.19 self-evaluated; no compared PPO baseline trained by the authors
No ablation of the random-vs-lowest rejected-response choice

terms.definition: distilled SFT: train the student on instructions and responses generated by a teacher
distilled DPO: DPO on teacher AI-feedback preference pairs from static data
AI Feedback: teacher (GPT-4) scores of four model responses per prompt, binarised into preferences

lineage.note: pipeline stages followed; ablation replicates that RLHF needs SFT first
lineage.quote: we replicate past results (Ouyang et al., 2022)
